passages.original: Adversus ipsam commutationem locorum de- tractis ceteris incommodis, quae exilio adhaerent, satis hoc remedii putat Varro, doctissimus Romanorum, quod, quocumque venimus, eadem rerum natura utendum est. M. Brutus satis hoc putat, quod licet in exilium euntibus virtutes suas secum ferre.
passages.english: Against the change of place itself, setting aside the other disadvantages that cling to exile, Varro, the most learned of the Romans, thinks this a sufficient remedy: that wherever we come, we have the same nature of things to make use of. Marcus Brutus thinks this sufficient: that those going into exile are permitted to carry their virtues with them.
